- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 2955-2957 (docstring of `_linked_pr_is_issue_implementation`), compared against line 2902 (`_linked_prs_by_body_reference`) and line 2979 (the predicate's own grep)
  Problem: The docstring claims the body close-keyword matcher is "the same pattern _linked_prs_by_body_reference matches". It is not the same pattern: the enumeration helper at line 2902 has no leading boundary (so `prefixes #77` matches there but is rejected by the predicate's `(^|[^[:alnum:]_-])` at line 2979), and its trailing boundary is Oniguruma `\b` (Unicode-aware) while the predicate uses the ASCII class `([^0-9A-Za-z_]|$)`. The asymmetry is deliberate and correct (the helper is a fail-open candidate enumeration; the predicate is the destructive-close authorization gate), but the "same pattern" wording states parity that does not exist.
  Why it fails at runtime: It does not fail at runtime — this is a comment-accuracy defect. The risk is maintenance-time: this exact docstring has already been through two accuracy-correction rounds on this PR (the branch-forms enumeration and the `cancel_zombie_runs_for_issue` boundary claim), and a future maintainer trusting "same pattern" could loosen the predicate's leading boundary to match the enumeration helper, which would let a body like `prefixes #77` authorize closing an unrelated PR. A one-line rewording such as "a stricter variant of the pattern _linked_prs_by_body_reference matches (adds a leading word boundary; ASCII trailing boundary)" removes the false parity claim.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
